panels.general_description: Paired genetic chromatogram columns compare a healthy control with both recipients.
panels.detailed_description: The right panel marked b has two columns, Exon 9 in a yellow heading and Exon 15 in a green heading. Each column contains two nucleotide sequence strings separated by a vertical mark beside conflict, with the differing letter colored red. Below are three rows labeled healthy control, recipient 1 and recipient 2; each row has a multicolored chromatogram trace with nucleotide letters above it. Red upward arrows mark the corresponding locus in both recipient traces. Footer labels are c.737G>A and Ser246Asn under Exon 9, and c.1468C>T and Arg490Cys under Exon 15. Peak axes have no numerical scale, unit or tick labels.

visual.general_description: Two recipient kidney-function courses with treatment and urine-marker displays.
visual.detailed_description: Panel a lies left and panel b right. Both use broken age axes and dual kidney-function axes; panel b adds dose bars and two lower urine-marker bar plots. Printed doses and selected visual estimates are distinguished.

panels.general_description: Recipient 1 clinical-course plot shows falling eGFR and rising creatinine with transplantation and dialysis annotations.
panels.detailed_description: The left panel a uses age along the horizontal axis with ticks 11, then a broken segment, then 18, 19 and 20. Left vertical axis is eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²), with ticks 0 to 120 in steps of 20; the right axis is Cre (mg/dL), with labeled ticks 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25. A gray eGFR segment descends from roughly the mid-30s near age 18 toward zero near 19; a black Cre line begins around 2–3 at 18, rises to about 4–5 and then about 24–25 near 19. A black downward arrow near 11 is labeled onset of proteinuria. A double-headed horizontal arrow across the 19–20 region is labeled hemodialysis. A downward KTx arrow lies near age 20; a genetic examination arrow lies farther right. The plot has no exact printed lab values attached to points.

evidence.quote:
Fig. 2.
Clinical courses of recipients 1 (a) and 2 (b). In recipient 1, kidney biopsy was not performed considering kidney atrophy, and she was lost to follow-up until end-stage kidney disease. She eventually underwent kidney transplantation (KTx) from her father. In recipient 2, proteinuria was identified at an earlier stage compared with that in recipient 1. Kidney biopsy and genetic examination were performed at the early stage of COQ8B nephropathy and CoQ10 supplementation was initiated followed by lisinopril. However, kidney function deteriorated as indicated by estimated glomerular filtration rate (gray line) and serum creatinine (Cre, black line) with marked increases in urinary protein (U-protein, black bars) and beta-2-microglobulin (U-β2MG, gray bars). KTx was performed from her mother at 4 years after initiating treatment.

caption_claims.value: Recipient 1 course includes deferred biopsy for kidney atrophy, loss to follow-up and transplantation from the father.

panels.general_description: Recipient 2 plot combines kidney-function curves, treatment-dose bars and urinary-marker bars.
panels.detailed_description: The right panel b has a large upper line plot with age ticks 8, an axis break, then 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16. Gray eGFR and black Cre curves use left eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²) and right Cre (mg/dL) axes. eGFR falls from about 120 to a low single-digit endpoint; Cre stays near the bottom for much of the course and rises steeply near KTx to below 20 mg/dL. Downward arrows mark onset of proteinuria, kidney biopsy, genetic examination and KTx. Stepped black CoQ10 bars across the top carry printed 5, 10, 20 and 30 with CoQ10 (mg/kg/day); a lower black bar reads lisinopril 2.5mg/day. Two narrow aligned bar plots below show gray U-β2MG (mg/gCre) with visible 0, 50 and 100 ticks, and black U-protein (g/gCre) with 0, 5 and 10 ticks. Both urine-marker sequences increase toward the right; the tallest gray terminal bar is roughly 60–70, and the highest terminal black bar roughly 9–10. Lower bars lack their own age tick labels.

evidence.quote:
Fig. 3.
Kidney biopsy findings of recipient 2 performed at 11 years of age. a Periodic acid-methenamine-silver (PAM) staining (×40) showing focal segmental glomerular sclerosis. b PAM staining (×400) of a segmentally sclerosed glomerulus in a magnified view. c Masson’s trichrome staining (×400) of tubular cells displaying granular swollen epithelial cells (arrowhead). d Numerous abnormal-shaped mitochondria were observed in the podocyte body at a high magnification by electron microscopy. Spiral arrows indicate podocyte microvillus transformation. Scale bar, 2.0 μm. e Podocyte foot process effacement was also noted (arrow). Scale bar, 2.0 μm.

panels.general_description: Grayscale electron micrograph with numerous dark oval profiles, yellow curved arrows and red-box inset.
panels.detailed_description: Panel d at upper right is grayscale ultrastructure, dominated on the right by many dark oval/elongated profiles with internal textures and pale intervening areas. A red box in the upper-right central region is linked by dotted red lines to an enlarged upper-left inset. Two yellow curved arrows point toward pale projections on the left side. A thick black horizontal scale bar lies near lower right.

evidence.quote:
Fig. 3.
Kidney biopsy findings of recipient 2 performed at 11 years of age. a Periodic acid-methenamine-silver (PAM) staining (×40) showing focal segmental glomerular sclerosis. b PAM staining (×400) of a segmentally sclerosed glomerulus in a magnified view. c Masson’s trichrome staining (×400) of tubular cells displaying granular swollen epithelial cells (arrowhead). d Numerous abnormal-shaped mitochondria were observed in the podocyte body at a high magnification by electron microscopy. Spiral arrows indicate podocyte microvillus transformation. Scale bar, 2.0 μm. e Podocyte foot process effacement was also noted (arrow). Scale bar, 2.0 μm.
A diagnosis of COQ8B nephropathy was confirmed based on genetic mutation patterns identical to those of her older sister.
